newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia calls presidential election for June 15.
newsitem.headline: Croatia calls presidential election for June 15.

text.p: The Croatian government on Monday set June 15 as the date for presidential elections in which President Franjo Tudjman has said he will run as candidate for the ruling Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ).
Although reported to be seriously ill, Tudjman, 74, still enjoys huge popularity in the country and is widely expected to romp home in the polls for another five-year term.

"The Croatian government made a unanimous decision in today's session to call the elections for the president of the Republic of Croatia for June 15 this year," it said in a statement to Croatia media.
Known as the "Father of the Nation" for declaring Croatian independence in 1991, Tudjman then led his country in a bitter war which spread throughout the former Yugoslavia.
He has been battling cancer since last year when he was treated in a U.S. hospital and observers say he is unlikely to last another full five-year term.

If he wins, Tudjman will preside over the recovery of the last piece of Croatian territory taken by Serbs in 1991 when Croatia seceded from Yugoslavia. Eastern Slavonia has been under United Nations administration since January last year and Tudjman is likely to treat its reintegration as a victory for independent Croatia.
